current.text: The Spurs started three guards (Harper, Fox and Castle) in the preseason and look set to keep doing it.
He is projected to come off the bench behind starters Fox, Harper, Castle, Vassell and Wembanyama.
The Spurs re-signed him for 3 years and 45 million.
Experts see no large enough role for him. San Antonio has too many players, and Dylan Harper's and Tobias Harris's minutes cut into his.
Do not consider him in 12-team formats. His ESPN rank of 112 is too high.
He would need a couple of injuries ahead of him to become a must-draft.
The Spurs roster is deep and its players had low minutes last season, so minutes may stay low after the long playoff run.
His jump in rim finishing is not expected to hold.
The Spurs play 3-4-3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks and have only 13 back-to-backs. The playoff schedule is okay but not great.

durable.text: He is a good three-point shooter and a good free throw shooter with okay rebounds and few turnovers. His steals and blocks are below average.
He is an undersized power forward, so teams with frontcourt size can hurt him on the glass.
His rim finishing rate rose from 60 to 71 percent, which is unusually high for a perimeter player.

note: At Yahoo rank 176 and an average cost of 1.0 USD (ESPN 0.5 USD), he sits outside our 144 drafted players and should go undrafted. ESPN's rank of 112 is too high for a projected bench forward. He adds threes, FT% and low turnovers, but his FG% (43.0) and points are below the pool and his steals and blocks are weak. Watch him on waivers early: check whether the three-guard lineup with Harper sticks and whether injuries to Harper, Vassell or Harris push him back toward the 27.6 minutes he played last season.
